Q: Window Vs GroupBy Performance in Spark A:

Many window function queries can be alternatively performed by aggregating data (i.e. groupBy) followed by join with the original data. Whether one approach will be faster than the other will be case by case, however, there is a simple heuristic that will guide the approach to take -- based off of your data and query.

If the cardinality of the key by which you will partitionBy (window function approach) or groupBy ("aggregating -> joining" approach) is large choose choose the former, and if it is small choose the latter.

Source: AWS Prescriptive Guidance

Another way to think about this:

  • if the original data is large and the aggregated data is large (because you aggregated by a high cardinality key) then choose window function approach

  • if the original data is large but the aggregated data is small (because you aggregated by a low cardinality key) then choose "aggregating -> joining" approach

Source:

https://youtu.be/9EIzhRKpiM8?si=GkmDO6IzfwkFQIEv&t=1105

https://stackoverflow.com/a/62434668/12609881

The tradeoff essentially boils down to:

  • window function approach -> less steps/stages but shuffling of more data

  • "aggregating -> joining" approach -> more steps/stages but shuffling of reduced data

Q: How to bold SPECIFIC TEXTS using "TEXTJOIN" or "CONCAT" formula A:

You cannot do this using formulas. Excel can only apply different formats to characters in a cell if the characters are part of an actual text string (NOT if they are the result of a formula).

To do this in Excel, you would need to write a VBA macro to

  • create the string
  • write the string to the cell
  • apply your bold formatting in the appropriate places using the Characters property of the Range object
